problems.title: Deployment redhat-ods-applications/kuberay-operator must be recreated: spec.selector cannot be changed
problems.description: The operator cannot apply its version of Deployment redhat-ods-applications/kuberay-operator because spec.selector is immutable; an older version created the object with a different value. The operator keeps failing until the object is deleted.
evidence: Reported by Ray default-ray, DataScienceCluster default-dsc

Failure deploying Deployment redhat-ods-applications/kuberay-operator (apps/v1): unable to patch apps/v1, Kind=Deployment redhat-ods-applications/kuberay-operator: Deployment.apps "kuberay-operator" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: {"matchLabels":{"app.kubernetes.io/component":"kuberay-operator","app.kubernetes.io/name":"kuberay"}}: field is immutable
problems.fix: Delete Deployment redhat-ods-applications/kuberay-operator, then restart redhat-ods-applications/ray-module-operator-controller-manager so it reconciles at once instead of after its back-off; the operator recreates it with the current spec and owner. Its pods stop until the operator recreates it; for a controller Deployment that is safe, because the operator recreates it with the current spec.
problems.technicalCmd: oc delete deployment.apps kuberay-operator -n redhat-ods-applications; oc rollout restart deployment/ray-module-operator-controller-manager -n redhat-ods-applications

problems.title: TrustyAI default-trustyai does not match its CRD's schema
problems.description: The live CRD and the object disagree on the type of a field, so the operator cannot update the object. This usually follows a downgrade or a round trip to an older version: OLM applies every CRD of the bundle it installs, so an older bundle replaces a same-named CRD, and a CRD the newer version no longer ships keeps the older schema after going back.
evidence: Reported by TrustyAI default-trustyai, DataScienceCluster default-dsc

Failure deploying TrustyAI default-trustyai (components.platform.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1): unable to patch components.platform.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1, Kind=TrustyAI /default-trustyai: failed to create typed live object (/default-trustyai; components.platform.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1, Kind=TrustyAI): errors: .spec.eval.lmeval.permitCodeExecution: expected boolean, got &{deny}
CRD trustyais.components.platform.opendatahub.io: spec.versions last written by catalog (Update) at 2026-10-05T12:00:00Z; OLM's catalog operator writes the CRDs of a bundle when it installs it
problems.fix: Re-apply trustyais.components.platform.opendatahub.io from the installed operator version's bundle, then correct the listed fields of TrustyAI default-trustyai to the type that CRD expects. The right value needs judgement, so there is no automatic fix. Afterwards restart redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager so it reconciles at once instead of after its back-off.
problems.technicalCmd: oc get trustyai.components.platform.opendatahub.io default-trustyai -o yaml; oc get crd trustyais.components.platform.opendatahub.io -o 'jsonpath={.metadata.managedFields}'; oc rollout restart deployment/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager -n redhat-ods-applications

problems.title: ServiceMonitor redhat-ods-applications/aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor has two controller owners
problems.description: Ownership of ServiceMonitor redhat-ods-applications/aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor moved between operator versions, and the object still carries the old controller reference, so the operator that owns it now cannot update it.
evidence: Failure deploying ServiceMonitor redhat-ods-applications/aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor (monitoring.coreos.com/v1): unable to patch monitoring.coreos.com/v1, Kind=ServiceMonitor redhat-ods-applications/aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor: ServiceMonitor.monitoring.coreos.com "aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor" is invalid: metadata.ownerReferences: Invalid value: [{"apiVersion":"config.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1","kind":"Platform","name":"default","uid":"1","controller":true},{"apiVersion":"components.platform.opendatahub.io/v1alpha1","kind":"AIHub","name":"default-aihub","uid":"2","controller":true}]...
problems.fix: Delete ServiceMonitor redhat-ods-applications/aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor, then restart the RHOAI operator (redhat-ods-operator/rhods-operator) so it reconciles at once instead of after its back-off; the operator recreates it with the current spec and owner. The operator recreates it on its next reconcile.
problems.technicalCmd: oc delete servicemonitor.monitoring.coreos.com aihub-controller-manager-metrics-monitor -n redhat-ods-applications; oc delete pod -n redhat-ods-operator -l name=rhods-operator
